regime_context: Detector shows a narrow, two-theme rotation (energy leading banks; only 4 of 17 themes eligible) with weak directional conviction (directional=false, absorption 0.46). The sole validated edge here is the absolute-trend gate, which is helping (gate_helps=true), so trend-eligible energy and high-dividend names deserve staying-power respect, while most everything else is below the discipline bar. No scorable ETF proxies exist for the leading themes, so virtually all options are low-conviction by construction.
emerging_watch: Watching whether Banks (H + HK) actually sustain a crowding retreat (crowding_z falling toward 0) AND a hurst_tag flip from mean-revert to trend. The condition that would retire this watch: energy's durability_bar drops below 0.6 while banks' breadth rises above 0.7 simultaneously.

theses.subject: Energy (H-shares)
theses.thesis: Energy is the only theme with a high durability bar (0.76), a strong trend tag (hurst_tag=trend), and broad participation (breadth 0.80) — the exact profile the validated absolute-trend gate is designed to stay with. theses.dissent: Energy's r10 (0.0217) is modest and the whole rotation is 'narrow' (only 24% of themes eligible), so leadership rests on very few names — a single large H-share energy stock can break the trend without index confirmation.

falsifier.text: Banks close the 0.136 score gap and overtake energy in rank before the check-by date, while energy breadth drops below 0.5

theses.subject: Banks (H + HK)
theses.thesis: Banks rank second on momentum (a focus lens only) but carry a crowded flag (crowded=true, z=1.09) — a size-down caution, not a short. More importantly, the hurst_tag is mean-revert (not trend), so the one validated edge (absolute-trend staying power) does not endorse it. The lean is expressed as a relative underweight against trend-qualified names, never a fade.

falsifier.text: Banks overtake energy in rank and their hurst_tag flips to trend while crowding_z falls below 0.5 before the check-by date
